title: plan-layer plan file
description: Shared state between a human developer and a coding agent. Every section is optional: the page renders only what is present, so a project can start with `plans` alone and grow into the rest. Fields not listed here are preserved in the file and ignored by the renderer and the gate, so a project can carry its own notes; a field that renders nowhere is still a field nobody reads.

plan_version.description: Bumped whenever the plan changes materially. Must match the newest changelog entry, and the gate fails when it does not. This is the version field; see `version` for the legacy duplicate.

updated.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Read from a clock, never from memory.

north_star.description: The goal the whole plan serves, rendered above the key. One sentence, changed rarely and deliberately.

north_star_owner.description: Who is allowed to change the north star. Naming an owner is what makes it frozen.

headings.description: Override any section heading and its hint text: { "systems": ["Environments", "hint text"] }. Keys are the section names the renderer uses: legend, figures, systems, capabilities, cycle, now, done, next, parked, edge_cases, invariants, glossary. The hint is the natural place to say what a section is carrying today, including a pointer to an archive file for the entries that were moved out of it.

version.description: LEGACY. An older name for the same number, kept because early plans wrote both. Nothing reads it. If it is present the gate drifts when it disagrees with plan_version, because two versions that differ mean one of them is wrong. Prefer plan_version alone.

north_star_frozen.description: A marker for readers of the file. Nothing reads it: the lock shown on the page comes from north_star_owner being present, not from this flag.

assertions_verified.description: ISO-8601 UTC stamp of the last `check.py --verify` run, written by hand after running it. Assertions declared but never recorded as run drift, and so does a stamp older than seven days, because a verified page that was verified a month ago is a claim about the past.

allow_multiple_active.description: Set true to allow more than one item in plans.now. The gate fails on a second active item otherwise: one thing in flight with its own checklist is what makes the page answer 'what is happening right now' in one glance.

mode.description: 0.16.0. 'light' is for short projects: the state file and the gate, without views, figures, live revision or rolling. Absent means full.

size_budget_kb.description: 0.16.0. The gate drifts when plan.json is larger than this many KB. Absent means 200.

contract.description: The obligation each side accepts. Stating it in the data beats a convention someone has to remember. Any key starting with `for_` is rendered, with a label derived from the name, so a project can address a named person as well as the agent and the human.

cycle.description: The stages every unit of work moves through. Omit to inherit the built-in six.

skipped_looks_like.description: The failure this stage exists to prevent. Write it from one you actually hit.

facts.description: Numbers quoted in more than one place, written once. Figures receive the whole plan and read data["facts"] instead of restating a value that also appears in the prose, so a picture cannot disagree with the table above it. The gate drifts when a figure asks for a fact that is not here, because the figure would draw a question mark that nobody re-reads.

systems.description: Environments you are moving between, side by side.

evidence.description: Required once build is anything but not-started. Progress claimed without evidence is the shape of a comfortable lie.

short.description: A shorter label for figures. A name that reads well in a table row overflows a diagram box, and abbreviating inside the renderer is the renderer guessing at wording it does not own.

done.description: Finished plans, oldest first. Two shapes are read, because an item is MOVED here rather than rewritten and is usually condensed later: the carried-over active shape (status, plan_file, tasks as a list) and the condensed archive shape (outcome, file, period, tasks as a summary string). The page prefers outcome over status and file over plan_file, so both render. Condense old entries into the archive shape and keep their full text in a sibling markdown file, named in the section's heading hint.

period.description: When the work ran, for example "28 Jul to 2 Aug". The gate drifts when a finished plan has none, because an undated record cannot be read in order.

outcome.description: What it produced, in one or two sentences. `status` is read in its place when the item still carries the active shape.

file.description: The plan document. `plan_file` is read in its place.

notable.description: What it taught us. Rendered under its own label, because the lesson outlives the task.

tasks.description: The checklist as it stood, or a summary string like "11 tasks" once condensed.

capability.description: Which capability it served. A capability with finished work filed against it cannot read as not-started.

task_columns.description: Carried over when a finished item was rendered as a table. Same shape as on an active item.

key.description: The field read off each task. Not name, state or note.

label.description: The column heading, in the reader's words.

status.description: Where the work actually stands, in prose. The page shows this under the item's name; the checklist shows the shape.

tasks.description: Flat checklist showing the shape of the plan and where it has got to. Individual steps belong in the plan document, not here.

note.description: Prose, or a list of points rendered as bullets under the step. A result's story is usually the time it ran and then what happened, which reads faster as points.

result.description: How the step turned out, which is not the same as where it sits in the run: a step can be done and have failed. pass, fail, covered and blocked are styled; any other word renders as written. Where any step in the item carries one, the table gains a leading Result column.

items.description: A step. Beyond name, state and note it may carry one key per declared task_columns entry, whose value fills that column's cell.

capability.description: Which capability this work serves. The gate fails on a reference that does not exist.

blocked_by.description: Names of other plan items this one waits on. Written here rather than in prose, because a dependency described only in a document cannot be checked — and that is how an item stayed active while its blocker sat unstarted.

why.description: Why this work, now. Carried when the item is promoted from next.

task_columns.description: Columns for the task checklist. Declare them when the checklist is something a person has to EXECUTE rather than read: the page then renders one row per step instead of a name with a paragraph under it. Each task may then carry these keys alongside name, state and note. A key may not be name, state or note, and may not repeat.

label.description: The column heading, in the reader's words.

capability.description: Which capability this work serves. The gate fails on a reference that does not exist.

blocked_by.description: Names of other plan items this one waits on. Written here rather than in prose, because a dependency described only in a document cannot be checked — and that is how an item stayed active while its blocker sat unstarted.

status.description: Not rendered on a queued item; the page shows why and unblocks. Written here it is invisible.

updated.description: Not rendered on a queued item. Kept when an item is demoted from now.

task_columns.description: Columns for the task checklist. Declare them when the checklist is something a person has to EXECUTE rather than read: the page then renders one row per step instead of a name with a paragraph under it. Each task may then carry these keys alongside name, state and note. A key may not be name, state or note, and may not repeat.

key.description: The field read off each task. Not name, state or note.

label.description: The column heading, in the reader's words.

parked.description: Questions deferred by decision, not oversight. Each names when it must be answered, so parked never quietly becomes dropped.

assertions.description: Claims the plan makes about the real system, each with a command that checks it. Run explicitly with check.py --verify; never from a hook, because they execute shell commands read from a repository file.

claim.description: The sentence on the page this command checks.

run.description: Shell command. Keep it trivial and read from $PLAN_FACTS; match locally.

expect.description: The exact stdout expected, or a regular expression when match is "regex".

refs.description: Where the claim appears, so a mismatch can be traced back to the sentence it disproves.

match.description: Set to "regex" to search `expect` in the output instead of comparing the whole string.

timeout.description: Seconds before the command is given up on. Default 60.

assertions_setup.description: One command run before the assertions; its stdout becomes $PLAN_FACTS, which each assertion then reads. One gather instead of many — eight separate connections once tripped a rate limit and locked the machine out of its own server.
